functions.funcDef: Provide thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subName: Generate forward thrust across the flight envelope
functions.subDef: Inputs: fuel at pump inlet, throttle/reverse commands from flight deck; processing: four podded turbofans with dual-channel FADEC; outputs: thrust, engine parameter data to AVI. Per §5.1.2/§5.1.4. Independence: left/right engine pairs in separate zones, services not commingled outboard of wing root (§5.1.5) — installation claim to test.

functions.funcDef: Provide thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subName: Provide reverse thrust for ground deceleration
functions.subDef: Inputs: reverse command, weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement; processing: thrust reversers on the two inboard engines with mechanical sleeve lock; outputs: reverse thrust on ground only. Per §5.1.2. Independence: in-flight deployment inhibited by WOW + RA agreement — interlock claim to test.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subName: Provide roll control
functions.subDef: Inputs: inceptor/autopilot command, HYD B and C, air/inertial data; processing: FBW via three dissimilar FCCs voting; outputs: two-segment aileron and spoiler position (§5.3.2/§5.3.4). Independence: ailerons on HYD B and C (§5.3.2) — dual-supply claim to test.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subName: Provide pitch control
functions.subDef: Inputs: inceptor/autopilot command, HYD A and C; processing: all-moving trimmable stabiliser with elevators, mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim; outputs: pitch surface position (§5.3.2). Independence: elevators on HYD A and C, mechanical reversion path to trim (§5.3.2) — claim to test.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subName: Provide yaw control
functions.subDef: Inputs: inceptor/autopilot command, HYD A (upper) and B (lower); processing: split rudder upper/lower segments each own actuation and supply, mechanical reversion to lower segment; outputs: rudder position (§5.3.2). Sizing case: outboard engine failure at V1 with max blade payload (§5.3.3). Independence: segments on separate supplies A and B — claim to test.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subName: Provide high-lift configuration
functions.subDef: Inputs: crew selection, hydraulic power; processing: double-slotted Fowler flaps in four sections and full-span slats via two independent PDUs through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes; outputs: high-lift position to performance computation (§5.3.2/§5.3.4). Independence: common torque shaft is a shared element (§5.3.2) — CMA candidate.

functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground and absorb landing/taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Support and absorb ground loads on semi-prepared surfaces
functions.subDef: Inputs: HYD A retraction/extension with free-fall alternate, gear lever; processing: one nose unit and six three-wheel main bogies (20 tyres), dual downlock sensing; outputs: gear position to flight deck, footprint pressure sized for flotation (§5.6.2). Preliminary: gear leg/bogie count not frozen (§1.2). Independence: dual independent downlock proximity circuits per unit (§5.6.2) — claim to test.

functions.funcDef: Provide braking and directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Provide wheel braking
functions.subDef: Inputs: HYD B normal / HYD A alternate / accumulator emergency, brake pedals/autobrake; processing: carbon multi-disc, electrically signalled hydraulically actuated, per-wheel-pair anti-skid; outputs: deceleration, brake temperature to AVI (§5.6.2). Sizing case: 1,800 m landing requirement vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout (§5.6.3). Independence: dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve (§5.6.3) — claim to test.

functions.funcDef: Provide braking and directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Provide ground directional control (steering)
functions.subDef: Inputs: tiller and rudder pedal command, hydraulic power; processing: nose wheel steering with mechanical disconnect for towing; outputs: nose wheel angle (§5.6.2). Independence: separate function from braking; steering/braking harnesses on opposite sides of each bay (§5.6.5) — claim to test.

functions.funcName: Provide hold access and pressure-boundary closure
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in hold access via the nose visor and form part of the pressure boundary when closed (SDD §5.7.1) — door structural load path is treated as structure, not a function (§5.7.3).
functions.subName: Actuate and lock the nose visor closed
functions.subDef: Inputs: HYD A visor drive plus electric backup, separate hydraulic supply to lock actuator, crew/ground command; processing: twelve rotary latches on a common torque shaft then eight independent locking pins; outputs: latch/lock engagement (§5.7.2). Independence: pins on a separate actuator and supply from latches (§5.7.2); latch common torque shaft is a shared element — CMA candidate.

functions.funcName: Provide hold access and pressure-boundary closure
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in hold access via the nose visor and form part of the pressure boundary when closed (SDD §5.7.1).
functions.subName: Sense and indicate lock status and inhibit unsafe unlock
functions.subDef: Inputs: pin position, pressurisation state from ECS; processing: two dissimilar independently routed sensing circuits (proximity harness + mechanical linkage), pressure interlock in series with unlock command; outputs: lock status to flight deck and take-off config monitor (§5.7.2/§5.7.4). Independence: dual dissimilar sensing on separated routes (§5.7.5); interlock confirms <0.1 psi before unlock (§5.7.2) — claims to test.

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t along the full hold length through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.8.1).
functions.subName: Maintain longitudinal blade restraint
functions.subDef: Inputs: electrical power to winches, loading/W&B data, WOW; processing: nine saddles with two tension straps each, electric winches locked mechanically, neighbour-carried load paths; outputs: strap tension to flight deck, restraint status to take-off config monitor (§5.8.2). Independence: loss of any one strap carried by neighbours (§5.8.3); no redundancy in hold floor hard points (§5.8.3 — structure). Note: monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop (§5.8.3).

functions.funcName: Condition and pressurise occupied and hold compartments
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subName: Control cabin/hold pressure differential
functions.subDef: Inputs: bleed air from four engines/APU via cross-bleed manifold, WOW, door position; processing: two digital controllers driving two outflow valves, pneumatic backup, independent mechanical relief; outputs: differential pressure and cabin altitude to AVI and crew oxygen logic, pressure state to nose door interlock (§5.9.2/§5.9.4). Preliminary: hold differential ~8,800 m equivalent not frozen (§1.2). Independence: two controllers/valves, either sufficient; relief independent of control (§5.9.2) — claim to test.

functions.funcName: Condition and pressurise occupied and hold compartments
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subName: Provide conditioned air to flight deck and hold
functions.subDef: Inputs: engine/APU bleed via cross-bleed manifold, ram air, electrical power; processing: two air cycle packs, two separate conditioning zones; outputs: conditioned air to flight deck and hold (§5.9.2). Independence: two packs, four bleed sources through cross-bleed manifold, either pack from either side (§5.9.3) — the shared cross-bleed manifold is a CMA candidate.

functions.funcName: Protect surfaces and sensors from ice
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes for flight in the icing envelope (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect wings and engine inlets from ice
functions.subDef: Inputs: bleed air from cross-bleed manifold, TAT/airspeed, crew/auto selection; processing: hot bleed air via piccolo distribution to wing leading edges and inlet cowls; outputs: ice protection status, bleed demand reducing pack capacity (§5.10.2/§5.10.4). Independence: bleed from either side via cross-bleed manifold (§5.10.3) — shared manifold is a CMA candidate.

functions.funcName: Protect surfaces and sensors from ice
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect stabiliser surfaces from ice
functions.subDef: Inputs: AC/DC electrical power, controller command; processing: electrically heated horizontal and vertical stabiliser leading edges in six independently controlled zones; outputs: zone health to AVI (§5.10.2). Independence: zones independently supplied, lost zone annunciated (§5.10.3) — claim to test.

functions.funcName: Protect surfaces and sensors from ice
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Heat probes, ports and windshields and detect ice
functions.subDef: Inputs: electrical power, crew/auto selection; processing: electrically heated probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors individually monitored; outputs: ice detection advisory to flight deck (§5.10.2). Independence: two ice detectors of the same type — commonality recorded for examination (§5.10.3) — CMA candidate.

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Acquire and present flight, navigation and system information
functions.subDef: Inputs: air data/inertial from three reference units, data from every system, navigation signals, electrical power; processing: three display processors on dual redundant deterministic network, dual FMC; outputs: displays, autopilot/autothrottle commands, recorded parameters (§5.11.2/§5.11.4). Independence: independent integrated standby instrument on DC essential sharing no supply/sensor/processing with primaries (§5.11.2) — claim to test.

functions.funcDef: Host the alerting that tells the crew what has failed and what to do (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Consolidate and present crew alerts and procedures
functions.subDef: Inputs: status from every aircraft system; processing: consolidation into a single prioritised crew alert list driven by two independent processing channels; outputs: prioritised alerts and associated procedures to the crew (§5.11.2). Independence: two independent processing channels (§5.11.2) — claim to test.

functions.funcName: Detect and suppress fire and overheat
functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subName: Detect fire and overheat in monitored zones
functions.subDef: Inputs: DC essential power, zone thermal state; processing: dual-loop continuous detection per engine nacelle and APU with AND logic degrading to single-loop, overheat detection on bleed ducts and gear bays, smoke detection at nine hold stations; outputs: fire/overheat warnings to crew alerting (§5.12.2). Independence: dual loops routed on opposite sides of each zone (§5.12.5). Assumption to substantiate: hold has detection but no suppression (§5.12.2).

functions.funcName: Detect and suppress fire and overheat
functions.funcDef: Provide the means to extinguish or suppress fire (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subName: Extinguish fire in engine and APU zones
functions.subDef: Inputs: hot battery bus discharge power, crew fire-handle command, APU state/WOW; processing: two cross-plumbed bottles per engine pair (either into either nacelle), single automatic APU bottle when unattended; outputs: discharge status, automatic APU shutdown and fuel isolation (§5.12.2/§5.12.4). Independence: discharge circuits on hot battery bus so available with all generation lost (§5.12.5). No hold suppression fitted (§5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and for the descent and diversion that follow (SDD §5.13.1).
functions.subName: Supply oxygen to flight-crew mask stations
functions.subDef: Inputs: cabin altitude signal from ECS, crew donning action, DC power for indication only; processing: two HP gaseous cylinders on a common manifold with crossover, four quick-donning demand-regulated masks; outputs: oxygen to four mask stations, cylinder pressure/low-pressure alerting to flight deck (§5.13.2/§5.13.4). Independence: two cylinders with crossover, either sufficient at reduced reserve; regulators independent per mask (§5.13.3). No passenger oxygen — hold unoccupied (§5.13.2).

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change without crew command
fha.effAc: An uncommanded thrust change alters the trajectory the crew commanded; if asymmetric across the four engines it introduces a yawing/rolling moment (outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the directional-control sizing case) demanding rudder authority to counter. Magnitude, symmetry and number of engines affected are not stated, so the worst-case aircraft effect cannot be bounded.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect an unexpected thrust/trajectory deviation and must intervene to restore the commanded state.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify without bounding the condition: the malfunction as stated does not fix magnitude, symmetry, or number of engines affected. An uncommanded asymmetric change on an outboard engine could approach the directional-control sizing case (potentially Hazardous+), while a small symmetric change may be Minor. Need the aspect/scope of the uncommanded change to derive severity from effects.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Thrust response not matching crew command
fha.effAc: Delivered thrust differs from the commanded value, so the achieved trajectory/energy state departs from what the crew commanded. If the mismatch is asymmetric across engines it loads directional control (outboard moment arm 28 m is the sizing case). The magnitude and symmetry of the mismatch are not stated, so the aircraft effect cannot be bounded.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe thrust/energy not tracking their command and must adjust or intervene.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the condition does not fix the size, direction, or symmetry of the mismatch. Ranges from a nuisance (Minor) to an asymmetric case approaching the directional-control sizing case. Need the aspect/magnitude of the mismatch to derive severity from effects.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded thrust drift developing below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: A slow drift below the crew detection threshold means the crew take no corrective action (unaware case), so the deviation accumulates unopposed; the trajectory/energy state departs progressively from that commanded. Whether the drift is symmetric or asymmetric, and its ultimate magnitude, are not stated, so the accumulated aircraft effect cannot be bounded.
fha.effCrew: By definition below the crew detection threshold; crew continue normal duties and take no action regarding it.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the unaware, undetected drift could accumulate to an asymmetric or energy-state condition of significant severity, but the material does not state the drift's direction, symmetry, saturation limit, or the point at which it becomes detectable/annunciated. Need the drift end-state and any annunciation to derive severity from effects.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced thrust available across the envelope
fha.effAc: Thrust is available but reduced, degrading climb, acceleration and energy margins across the envelope; performance-limited phases (take-off, climb, go-around) are most affected. The aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following loss of any one engine, but the degree of reduction here is not stated, so the effect cannot be bounded against that design case.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe reduced performance/thrust and manage the energy state, potentially amending the flight profile or diverting.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: 'reduced' does not fix the magnitude of the loss. A small reduction may be Minor; a reduction approaching or exceeding the one-engine-inoperative design case in a performance-limited phase could be Major or worse. Need the degree of thrust reduction and affected phase to derive severity from effects.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust, remaining thrust insufficient to maintain level flight
fha.effAc: Remaining thrust is insufficient to maintain level flight, forcing an unavoidable descent regardless of crew action; the aircraft cannot hold altitude and, absent a reachable landing site, cannot sustain flight to a suitable aerodrome. This exceeds the one-engine-inoperative design continuation case (continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine).
fha.effCrew: Crew face a forced descent they cannot arrest with thrust; workload dominated by energy management, terrain avoidance and diversion/forced-landing to the nearest suitable site.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. Thrust insufficient to maintain level flight means an unavoidable descent the crew cannot arrest, exceeding the stated one-engine-inoperative continuation design case; over terrain or beyond glide of a suitable surface this drives toward a hull loss. Catastrophic ↔ Extremely Improbable (1e-9/fh) per Part 25. Confirm scope and whether a reachable suitable surface can mitigate in relevant phases. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric loss of forward thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm
fha.effAc: Large yawing/rolling moment about the 28 m outboard arm; requires rudder authority to maintain directional control; performance degraded but continued flight to a suitable aerodrome is a design case.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply rudder and asymmetric-thrust drill; increased workload; failed engine isolated via fuel shut-off and fire handle.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: SDD makes outboard-engine failure at V1 with max blade payload the directional-control sizing case and states continued flight to a suitable aerodrome following loss of any one engine; effects are significant handling/workload with retained control, supporting Major (proposed). Confirm against §25.1309; if single-engine controllability is not in fact assured at the sizing case, severity increases. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust generation (all four engines)
fha.effAc: Total loss of propulsive thrust; aircraft cannot sustain flight; forced descent/off-field landing with no thrust available.
fha.effCrew: Crew execute all-engine-out drill; extreme workload; no thrust for go-around or diversion.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of all forward thrust precludes continued flight; the effect (inability to sustain flight) supports Catastrophic (proposed), objective Extremely Improbable / 1e-9/fh under Part 25. Confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent reverse thrust deployment in flight (inboard engine)
fha.effAc: Reverser deployment on an inboard engine in flight; the aircraft-level upset/controllability outcome is not characterised in the provided material.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states in-flight reverser deployment is inhibited by WOW + radio-altimeter agreement + a mechanical sleeve lock, but does NOT state the aircraft-level effect (asymmetric drag/yaw magnitude, controllability, or recoverability) of an in-flight inboard-reverser deployment. Without a stated aircraft effect this condition cannot be classified — the effect on controllability and the flight phase of greatest exposure are missing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reverse thrust applied on the ground without crew command (inboard engine)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded reverse on an inboard engine on the ground; asymmetric deceleration/thrust; the magnitude of directional-control disturbance and stopping-margin impact is not characterised in the provided material.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only, so an uncommanded ground deployment would be asymmetric; however the SDD does not state the aircraft-level effect (directional excursion, stopping distance against the 1,800 m / ~1,080 m margin) of an uncommanded single-inboard reverse on the ground, so the condition cannot be classified without that effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced reverse thrust available on the ground
fha.effAc: Reduced reverse-thrust contribution to ground deceleration; increased reliance on wheel braking against the landing-distance margin (1,800 m requirement vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface).
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum wheel braking; increased workload; may need to manage remaining stopping margin.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Reverse thrust supports ground deceleration and the operating margin on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip; but the provided material does not quantify how much of the stopping performance depends on reverse thrust versus wheel braking, so the effect on the landing-distance margin (and therefore severity) cannot be grounded. Confirm the credited reverse-thrust contribution to certified landing distance.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of reverse thrust for ground deceleration
fha.effAc: Ground deceleration relies on wheel braking and spoilers alone; reverse thrust (inboard engines only) unavailable. Predicted rollout ~1,080 m against an 1,800 m semi-prepared landing distance requirement, so stopping margin is reduced but braking/spoiler capability remains.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum wheel braking within the retained margin; workload increased on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects support a significant reduction in safety margin / crew workload increase on landing rollout, not a Catastrophic/Hazardous loss, because the SDD states predicted rollout ~1,080 m against the 1,800 m requirement leaving braking margin. PROPOSED for engineer confirmation; the retained margin under degraded braking on a semi-prepared surface must be substantiated. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft rolls differently from the crew's roll command; a trajectory deviation results whose magnitude and recoverability depend on the error size and flight phase, which the function definition does not quantify.
