fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Backup mode retains differential control with conventional flight-deck cabin altitude maintained and independent mechanical relief intact; effect is a slight reduction in safety margin and a modest crew workload increase — Minor. Confirm backup-mode control accuracy is sufficient to hold flight-deck cabin altitude within limits. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Single-controller or single-outflow-path degradation: loss of one of two digital controllers or one of two outflow valves, either being sufficient
fha.effAc: Full automatic pressurisation control retained on the remaining controller/outflow valve; either valve is sufficient
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated; no immediate crew action required to maintain pressurisation
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Redundant controller/outflow valve carries the function with no loss of capability; a slight reduction in remaining redundancy with annunciation — Minor. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pressure-differential control across the fuselage (automatic, backup and outflow control all lost)
fha.effAc: Loss of controlled differential; independent positive and negative pressure relief valves continue to protect the structure; uncontrolled cabin altitude excursion possible up to ambient at cruise level
fha.effCrew: Flight deck loses conventional cabin altitude control; crew don oxygen and initiate emergency descent from up to FL260; high workload
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Independent mechanical relief protects structure, but uncontrolled flight-deck cabin altitude excursion at up to FL260 imposes an emergency descent under oxygen with high crew workload — proposed Hazardous. Not classified Catastrophic because structure is protected by independent relief and the hold is unoccupied. Confirm: crew oxygen endurance and emergency-descent capability from FL260 bound the flight-deck occupant outcome; hold differential is preliminary and could shift this classification. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Conditioned-air temperature or flow to flight deck and hold outside required limits
fha.effAc: Conditioned-air supply present but temperature or flow out of required band; pressurisation and pack function otherwise available
fha.effCrew: Flight-deck thermal/flow environment degraded; crew may reconfigure packs/bleed source; increased workload
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided function definition establishes conditioned-air out of limits but does not characterise the magnitude of the flight-deck thermal/flow excursion or its effect on crew performance, so no aircraft-level effect severe enough to classify can be derived. Missing: bounds of the temperature/flow excursion and the resulting crew-performance impact (against HIDH workload/occupancy limits).. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Contaminant or temperature excursion in conditioned-air supply developing below the detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Undetected conditioned-air contaminant or temperature excursion progresses without annunciation; crew continue normal duties taking no corrective action
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; potential progressive degradation of flight-deck air quality affecting crew performance if excursion reaches an impairing level
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Crew-unaware case: the document establishes the excursion develops below detection but does not characterise the contaminant type, the level reached, or the effect on crew capability, so an aircraft-level effect cannot be derived and severity cannot be classified. Missing: nature/severity of the excursion and crew-incapacitation potential before any independent cue (e.g. crew oxygen use) intervenes.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of conditioned-air supply: loss of one air-cycle pack with the remaining pack on a reduced conditioning schedule
fha.effAc: One pack lost; remaining pack supplies flight deck and hold on a reduced conditioning schedule. Single-pack operation is a permitted degraded state.
fha.effCrew: Crew reconfigure to single-pack operation; conditioning schedule reduced but conditioned air remains available to the flight deck.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD states single-pack operation is permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule but does not state the resulting flight-deck cabin-altitude or temperature effect, so no aircraft/crew effect severe enough to classify can be derived. Need the single-pack conditioning performance (flight-deck cabin altitude / temperature limits) to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of conditioned-air supply to flight deck and hold
fha.effAc: No conditioned air to flight deck or hold; pressurisation depends on the pressurisation-control function (SF-013) and structural relief. Independent mechanical relief and pneumatic backup govern pressure state.
fha.effCrew: Flight deck loses conditioning; crew workload increases to manage descent and, if cabin altitude is not maintained, to don oxygen (crew oxygen is a separate function, SF-022).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Complete loss of conditioned air affects the occupied flight deck, but the SDD does not state the resulting flight-deck cabin-altitude excursion or the time available before it becomes a crew-incapacitation concern, and pressurisation control is a separate function. Cannot derive a defensible severity without the cabin-altitude effect and the crew-oxygen coverage interaction. Requires pressurisation/cabin-altitude analysis to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Malfunction: wing and engine-inlet ice protection active when not required, imposing a performance penalty
fha.effAc: Bleed-air ice protection active when not required draws bleed that reduces pack capacity and imposes a performance penalty; the displayed performance penalty of wing anti-ice in use is applied automatically.
fha.effCrew: Crew see ice-protection status and applied performance penalty on the displays; may deselect if in manual, or the condition persists in automatic.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD states wing anti-ice in use imposes a performance penalty and reduces pack capacity, and that the penalty is displayed and applied automatically, but does not quantify the penalty or state any resulting margin loss against a critical performance case, so an aircraft-level effect severity cannot be derived. Need the magnitude of the performance penalty relative to sizing/dispatch margins.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ice protection: loss of ice protection to wings or engine inlets on one side
fha.effAc: Ice protection to one side's wing/inlets lost; SDD states bleed protection is available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold, and a lost condition is annunciated. In icing, unprotected surface on one side accretes ice, giving asymmetric aerodynamic/ingestion effects.
fha.effCrew: Crew annunciated of the lost protection; ice detection is advisory. Crew action to exit icing or reconfigure bleed is required.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD states cross-bleed makes bleed protection available from either side and that a lost zone is annunciated, but does not state the aerodynamic or engine-ingestion effect of asymmetric ice accretion in the icing envelope, so the aircraft effect cannot be characterised well enough to classify. Need the handling/performance/ingestion consequence of one-side unprotected accretion in the certification icing envelope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced wing and engine-inlet ice protection capability, with the bleed demand for anti-ice reducing environmental pack conditioning capacity
fha.effAc: Ice protection remains available but at reduced capability in the icing envelope; concurrent reduction in pack conditioning capacity when anti-ice is in use. Performance penalty is applied to displayed performance.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via zone health/status and the applied performance penalty; may need to limit exposure to icing conditions and manage pack configuration.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive the aircraft outcome from the provided definitions alone: the icing envelope of the certification basis and the actual protection shortfall / residual accretion consequence are not quantified in the SDD, so whether reduced-but-available protection with a pack-capacity trade is Minor or Major is not groundable. Needs icing certification basis and performance-margin data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of wing and engine-inlet ice protection with ice detection unavailable, crew continuing normal duties and taking no action
fha.effAc: Protection is lost on wings and/or inlets while the crew are unaware because ice detection is unavailable; ice may accrete on protected surfaces and inlets in the icing envelope with no annunciation and no performance penalty applied.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue normal duties and take no action regarding the loss; no cue that ice protection has failed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The latent-loss aircraft consequence (aerodynamic degradation / inlet ice ingestion severity) is not stated in the SDD and depends on the icing certification envelope not defined here; a plausible-but-ungrounded severity is withheld. The undetected/unannunciated character (detection advisory, two detectors of the same type) makes this the worst-case awareness split and likely more severe than the annunciated cases — confirm against the icing basis before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of wing and engine-inlet ice protection in the icing envelope of the certification basis
fha.effAc: No protection of wing leading edges or engine inlet cowls; in the icing envelope ice accretes on lift-producing surfaces and engine inlets, degrading aerodynamic performance and threatening inlet/engine operation.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via ice protection status; assumed to exit icing conditions per procedure; increased workload managing an exit from icing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft outcome of total protection loss in icing (magnitude of performance loss, inlet ice-ingestion consequence, and whether exit from icing is always achievable) is not quantified in the provided material; the icing certification envelope is not defined here. Severity withheld rather than guessed — needs the icing basis and aero/engine substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous stabiliser zone heating with no crew command (unwanted heating active on one or more of the six stabiliser zones)
fha.effAc: One or more stabiliser heating zones active when not required, imposing an electrical load and thermal input on stabiliser surfaces without command; no loss of stabiliser protection itself.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via zone health/annunciation; may deselect or manage the affected zone.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft-level consequence of unwanted electrical stabiliser heating (any structural/thermal or electrical-load effect) is not characterised in the provided material; the SDD gives architecture only. Without a stated adverse effect, no §25.1309 class can be derived and none is assumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Insufficient stabiliser heating against active ice accretion — heating commanded/active but inadequate to prevent or remove accretion on the stabiliser leading edges
fha.effAc: Ice accretes on the horizontal/vertical stabiliser leading edges despite heating, degrading tail effectiveness and pitch/yaw control margins in the icing envelope.
fha.effCrew: May be unaware if a heating zone reports healthy while output is inadequate; if annunciated, assumed to exit icing conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The handling-quality / controllability consequence of stabiliser ice accretion is not quantified in the provided material and depends on the icing certification envelope not defined here; whether inadequate heating with residual accretion is Major or Hazardous cannot be grounded. Severity withheld rather than reaching for a mid-scale value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected stabiliser ice accretion below annunciation threshold (crew unaware, no protective action taken)
fha.effAc: Ice accretes on stabiliser leading edges without annunciation; tailplane effectiveness and longitudinal stability/control margin degrade progressively; risk of reduced pitch control authority or tailplane stall, most acute in the approach/configuration-change regime.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties with no cue to activate or verify protection; degraded pitch response may not be attributed to ice until control difficulty manifests.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; not applicable to passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Unaware tailplane ice accretion degrading longitudinal control with no crew action available; consistent with a large reduction in safety margins / difficulty in control per the Hazardous examples. Proposed for engineer confirmation; the actual pitch-control degradation magnitude for this stabiliser requires aerodynamic substantiation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one or more stabiliser heating zones (partial loss, remaining zones protected, lost zone annunciated)
fha.effAc: One or more of the six independently controlled stabiliser zones unprotected; localised ice accretion possible in the affected zone with reduced but not lost stabiliser effectiveness; remaining zones continue to protect.
fha.effCrew: Lost zone annunciated; crew can restrict flight in icing conditions, exit icing, or apply icing procedures.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; not applicable to passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Annunciated partial loss of stabiliser protection with residual protection and crew procedural options; proposed Major pending confirmation. The aircraft-level effect of a single unprotected zone (whether it degrades handling significantly) requires aerodynamic substantiation to confirm the class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of stabiliser ice protection (all six zones unavailable)
fha.effAc: No protection to horizontal or vertical stabiliser leading edges; unrestricted ice accretion in the icing envelope degrades tailplane effectiveness, longitudinal stability and pitch control authority, with risk of tailplane stall in the approach/configuration-change regime.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated; crew must exit icing conditions and apply icing procedures; sustained icing exposure leaves no protective means.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; not applicable to passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of stabiliser protection in the icing envelope degrading longitudinal control; proposed Hazardous on a large reduction in safety margins. Whether annunciation plus crew avoidance reduces this below Hazardous, or accretion severity drives it higher, requires aerodynamic and operational substantiation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: False ice detection advisory with no accretion present
fha.effAc: Ice detection advisory presented with no actual accretion; if automatic activation is armed, protection energised unnecessarily, imposing the performance penalty of anti-ice in use; no loss of any protective capability.
fha.effCrew: Crew presented with an unwarranted icing advisory; may select protection on or apply icing procedures unnecessarily; increased workload and possible unnecessary performance restriction.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; not applicable to passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Nuisance advisory with unnecessary but available protection activation and a performance penalty; slight increase in crew workload, no loss of function. Proposed Minor for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous heater activation with no crew command (probe/port/windshield heating energised uncommanded)
fha.effAc: Probe, port or windshield heating energised without command; imposes an electrical load and thermal input where not required; individually monitored so an anomalous element is detectable; no loss of air-data or protective capability.
fha.effCrew: Element health monitored individually; crew can observe status; minimal operational effect.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; not applicable to passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded heater activation of individually monitored elements with no loss of function; slight effect at most. Proposed Minor pending confirmation that uncommanded heating cannot damage a probe on the ground or corrupt air data — that requires substantiation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of probe, port and windshield heating and ice detection
fha.effAc: Probes, static ports and windshields lose heating and ice detection is lost concurrently; in the icing envelope unheated probes/ports can ice, corrupting air data (airspeed, altitude, AoA) that feeds displays and envelope protection, with no ice-detection cue to the crew.
fha.effCrew: Crew face potentially erroneous or unreliable air-data indications with degraded windshield visibility and no ice-detection advisory; increased workload identifying and managing unreliable air data.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. Simultaneous loss of probe/port/windshield heating and ice detection in the icing envelope can corrupt primary air data driving displays and envelope protection while removing the detection cue; effects support Hazardous (Severe-Major) — significant reduction in safety margins and higher crew workload — pending confirmation that redundant air-data sources and standby cannot fully compensate. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of individual probe or port heating
fha.effAc: A single probe or port loses heating and may ice in the icing envelope, producing an erroneous single air-data source; three air data inertial reference units and independent standby sensing remain available so the affected source can be identified and rejected.
fha.effCrew: Crew identify and manage a single miscompared/unreliable air-data source using remaining sources and standby; moderate increase in workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. Loss of one probe/port heater yields at most one corrupted air-data source against triple air-data plus an independent standby that shares no supply/sensor/processing, allowing detection and rejection; effects (reduction in margins, increased workload, no misleading undetected data) support Major, pending confirmation of monitoring/miscompare coverage. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of ice detection function only
fha.effAc: Ice detection is lost while probe, port and windshield heating remain available; the automatic detection cue and automatic activation are unavailable, but manual selection of ice protection remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew lose the ice-detection advisory and automatic activation, and must rely on other icing cues and manual selection of protection.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the aircraft-level effect turns on whether losing only the detection function (with heating intact and manual selection available) leaves surfaces adequately protected. The provided material states detection is advisory with manual and automatic-on selection but does not establish the crew procedure or the consequence of un-cued icing on unprotected surfaces — the resulting aircraft effect is not grounded in the function definition. Severity left EMPTY pending that input.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected probe or port icing corrupting air data below monitoring threshold
fha.effAc: Probe or port icing corrupts air data (airspeed, altitude, AoA) slowly below the monitoring/miscompare threshold, so corrupted data propagates to displays and envelope protection without triggering a miscompare or crew cue.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties acting on air data they believe valid; misleading indications may lead to inappropriate control inputs before the error is recognised.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. Undetected, below-threshold corruption of primary air data feeding displays and envelope protection is misleading data the crew act on unaware; per ARP4761A the unaware case can raise severity. Effects support Hazardous — potentially unsafe control inputs and reduced margins before recognition — pending confirmation of triple-source miscompare coverage against slow common-mode icing. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of ice detection with icing present
fha.effAc: Ice detection is lost undetected while icing conditions are present, so accretion on protected surfaces/inlets proceeds without any detection cue and without automatic activation of protection.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware detection has failed and icing is accreting; protection may not be selected on in time absent other icing cues.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. Undetected loss of detection with icing present removes the crew's primary cue to activate protection, allowing un-cued accretion; the unaware condition supports Hazardous — significant reduction in safety margins if protection is not selected in time — pending confirmation of independent icing cues and detector redundancy/monitoring. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous flight or navigation information presented to crew
fha.effAc: Aircraft controlled to erroneous flight/navigation reference; potential deviation from intended flight path, unsafe attitude/speed/track before crew reconciles against independent standby.
fha.effCrew: Crew acts on erroneous primary indication; alerting is dual-channel and an independent standby (attitude/airspeed/altitude) is available for cross-check, but reconciliation is workload-intensive and may be delayed in high-workload phases.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight)
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous flight/navigation information acted upon can produce an unsafe flight-path/attitude deviation; the independent standby that shares no supply, sensor or processing enables crew detection and reversion, which typically bounds this away from Catastrophic to Hazardous. Proposed for confirmation — degree of misleading vs annunciated-erroneous distinguishes M from M3. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous system information presented to crew
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight)
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the aircraft function is defined as 'acquire and present flight, navigation and system information' but does not identify WHICH system parameters are presented or which are safety-relevant. Effect on aircraft/crew depends entirely on the specific erroneous system datum (e.g. fuel quantity, gear status, fire status) — not grounded at aircraft level. Needs the system-information content set to state an aircraft effect and derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Misleading flight or navigation information within tolerance, not cross-monitored
fha.effAc: Aircraft flown to a subtly wrong reference that stays within monitoring tolerance and is not annunciated; slow accumulation of flight-path/navigation error not caught by cross-monitor, with potential unsafe deviation particularly in approach/landing.
fha.effCrew: Crew has no alert and no ready trigger to consult the standby because the error is within tolerance and not cross-monitored; detection relies on crew noticing external cues, which may not occur before an unsafe condition develops.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight)
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misleading-and-undetected information is the classical driver toward the more severe end because the crew is not cued to reject it; absence of cross-monitor removes the standby benefit. Whether Hazardous or Catastrophic depends on the parameter and phase and on whether ANY independent cue exists — proposed as Hazardous pending confirmation of monitoring coverage. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of a presented parameter
fha.effAc: A required flight/navigation parameter ceases to be presented without annunciation; aircraft flown without that reference, with effect depending on which parameter is silently lost and the phase.
fha.effCrew: Crew is unaware the parameter is missing/frozen; no alert cues reversion to standby, so the crew continues normal duties without the datum until an external cue or degraded outcome reveals it.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight)
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected (unannunciated) loss of a presented parameter denies the crew the trigger to revert to the independent standby; severity is driven by which parameter is lost undetected and in which phase. Proposed Hazardous pending identification of the specific parameter set and monitoring — a critical primary parameter lost undetected in approach could argue Catastrophic. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary display with standby available
fha.effAc: Primary flight/navigation display presentation lost; aircraft continues to be flown on the independent standby attitude/airspeed/altitude with reduced information and increased crew workload.
fha.effCrew: Loss is detected (display blank/failed); crew reverts to the independent standby instrument and reversionary display selection (manual), continuing safe flight and landing with reduced situational information and elevated workload.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight)
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Detected loss of the primary display with an available, fully independent standby (no shared supply/sensor/processing) leaves a safe but degraded means of flight with increased crew workload — the standard signature of Major. Proposed for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: complete loss of flight, navigation and system information display
fha.effAc: Primary display suite unavailable; an independent standby instrument sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries provides attitude, airspeed and altitude, permitting continued flight on standby data.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses consolidated flight/nav/system presentation and reverts to the standby instrument; increased workload to fly and navigate on minimal data; alerting availability depends on separate channels.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Hazardous for engineer confirmation: total loss of primary presentation with a surviving independent standby (attitude/airspeed/altitude) degrades capability and materially raises crew workload but is not shown to preclude continued safe flight and landing; grounded in the SDD standby-instrument independence claim. Confirm against the workload↔severity ladder and against night/IMC exposure before freezing. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: loss of a subset of presented information
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the condition is named in this turn's instruction but is NOT an existing FCIM condition for SF-018 (SF-018 carries TL, PL, M and M3 only), and the SDD does not identify WHICH subset of information is lost. Without knowing whether the lost subset is safety-critical (e.g. attitude vs a secondary system page), no aircraft effect can be grounded and no severity derived. Engineer to confirm the condition exists and define the subset.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: degraded to standby attitude, airspeed and altitude only
fha.effAc: Primary presentation lost; aircraft flown on the independent standby instrument providing attitude, airspeed and altitude only, with no primary navigation, systems or consolidated presentation.
fha.effCrew: Crew flies on standby attitude/airspeed/altitude with substantially increased workload; navigation and system-status awareness degraded; procedures and alerting depend on separate channels.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects grounded from the standby-instrument architecture, but severity left blank: the SDD does not quantify the crew-workload penalty of flying standby-only nor the exposure (night/IMC, sector length, diversion), so the workload↔severity classification cannot be derived without engineering judgement. Not benign — do not read the blank as No Safety Effect. Engineer to assess workload against the AC 25.1309 ladder.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: spurious or false crew alert presented
fha.effCrew: Crew presented with an alert for a condition that does not exist; potential nuisance workload and risk of inappropriate crew response to a non-existent condition; the consolidated prioritised alert list is driven by two independent processing channels.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity left blank: the aircraft-level consequence of a spurious alert depends on WHICH alert and on the crew action it induces (a false fire/engine warning versus a benign advisory drive very different outcomes), and the SDD does not enumerate alert criticality or the induced-error potential. Cannot derive a §25.1309 class from the description alone; do not default to No Safety Effect. Engineer to define the worst-case spurious alert and its induced action.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: incorrect alert prioritisation presented
fha.effCrew: Crew presented with alerts in an incorrect priority order, risking attention to a lower-consequence condition ahead of a higher-consequence one, or delayed recognition of a time-critical condition; alerting is driven by two independent processing channels.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity left blank: the consequence of mis-prioritisation depends on which higher-consequence alert is masked or delayed and on the available time-to-act, none of which the SDD quantifies. A misleading/mis-prioritised alert on a time-critical condition could be severe, so the blank must not be read as benign. Engineer to identify the worst-case masked condition and its time criticality before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: complete loss of crew alerting and procedure presentation
fha.effAc: Aircraft continues to fly, but the crew receives no consolidated alerting of system failures and no associated procedures; subsequent failures go unannunciated and unmanaged, defeating the assumption that the crew is alerted to and can act on degradations.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and diagnose all failures unaided and without procedural guidance, a substantial increase in workload and a marked reduction in ability to manage a failed condition correctly.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of consolidated alerting and procedures removes the crew's primary means of recognising and managing subsequent failures; effects support Hazardous (Severe-Major) — a large reduction in safety margins with crew workload/ability impaired. Proposed only; confirm against §25.1309 ladder and confirm whether standby/independent annunciation of the most critical warnings survives this condition (which could lower it). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: failure to annunciate a valid condition (missed alert)
fha.effAc: A genuine failure or unsafe state is not annunciated; the aircraft may continue in an undetected degraded or hazardous configuration with no crew prompt to act, the effect depending on which condition is missed.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware of an active condition and take no corrective action; the safety margin lost is that of the underlying missed condition, compounded by the absence of any prompt.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity cannot be grounded from the function definition alone: the effect of a missed alert depends entirely on WHICH condition is not annunciated (a missed fire warning vs a missed minor advisory span the whole scale). The provided function definition ('Consolidate and present crew alerts and procedures') does not identify the specific alerts, so no single aircraft-level effect can be stated. Requires the alert criticality set / worst-case missed condition to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: suppressed or omitted procedure for an active condition
fha.effAc: An alert is presented but its associated procedure is missing or wrong; the condition is recognised but the crew is not correctly guided to manage it, the aircraft effect depending on the condition whose procedure is omitted.
fha.effCrew: Crew are aware a condition is active but lack correct procedural guidance to address it, increasing the likelihood of an incorrect or delayed response; workload increased.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on which active condition's procedure is suppressed and whether the crew can manage it from training/memory without the displayed procedure; the provided function definition does not identify the procedure set or a worst case, so no aircraft-level effect can be fixed. Requires the associated procedure set / worst-case condition to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: loss of one alerting processing channel
fha.effAc: One of two independent alerting processing channels is lost; consolidated alerting and procedures remain available on the surviving channel, with reduced redundancy and no loss of the annunciated function.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain full alerting and procedure presentation; loss is annunciated as a system status with reduced redundancy, minor increase in monitoring awareness only.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With two independent processing channels (SDD §5.11.2 'driven by two independent processing channels'), loss of one leaves the alerting function fully available on the other; effects are a slight reduction in redundancy — Minor. Proposed only; confirm the surviving channel provides full coverage and that the loss is annunciated. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: loss of associated procedure display with alerts retained
fha.effAc: Crew alerts continue to be presented but the associated procedures are no longer displayed; the crew is still told what has failed but must manage it from training and paper/memory procedures, a partial capability reduction.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain awareness of active conditions but lose on-display procedural guidance; slight to moderate increase in workload, mitigated by trained/backup procedures.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Classification hinges on whether an independent backup procedure means (paper checklist / trained memory items) is assumed available with the crew still alerted; the provided material does not state the procedure-backup provision, so the aircraft effect and severity cannot be grounded. Requires the backup-procedure assumption to classify (if a full paper/QRH backup exists this trends Minor; if not, worse).. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: False fire or overheat warning presented with no fire present
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Spurious fire/overheat warning may prompt crew to shut down and discharge into a healthy engine/APU, reducing available thrust and, on an outboard engine, imposing the sizing asymmetric-thrust case; on a four-engine aircraft one erroneous shutdown is a degraded but continued-flight state.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload and diagnostic burden; risk of unnecessary engine shutdown and extinguishant discharge in response to a false warning.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; freighter carries flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from effects: a false warning driving an unnecessary single-engine shutdown/discharge is a significant reduction in safety margin and crew workload but four-engine architecture supports continued safe flight and landing; PROPOSED for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to detect an actual fire or overheat in a monitored zone
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: An undetected fire/overheat in an engine nacelle, APU compartment, bleed-duct run or gear bay progresses without warning and without crew-commanded extinguishing, permitting uncontrolled fire propagation through a fire zone containing flammable fluid and high-energy sources.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no warning and takes no protective action; first indication is secondary effects, by which point the fire may be uncontained.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; freighter carries flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from effects: undetected fire in a designated fire zone with flammable fluid, defeating the crew-commanded extinguishing path, can lead to uncontrolled fire and loss of the aircraft; PROPOSED for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire/overheat detection in one or more monitored zones (remaining zones detected)
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Fire/overheat in the affected zone(s) would go undetected while other zones retain detection; a fire in an unmonitored zone progresses without warning, though coverage of the remaining fire zones is retained.
fha.effCrew: No warning for the affected zone; crew unaware of loss of coverage unless annunciated; no protective action for a fire in that zone.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; freighter carries flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from effects: loss of detection over one or more fire zones removes the warning that enables crew extinguishing, materially reducing safety margin for a fire event in the affected zone; PROPOSED for confirmation. Whether loss is annunciated to the crew is not stated for this condition. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degradation to single-loop detection logic in a monitored zone (loss of one detection loop)
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Detection reverts from dual-loop AND logic to single-loop logic in the affected zone; warning capability is retained but the effect on detection integrity (increased susceptibility to spurious warning and/or reduced confirmation) is not quantified in the provided description.
fha.effCrew: Detection remains available in the affected zone on single-loop logic; residual crew impact depends on the change in warning integrity, not stated.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; freighter carries flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from provided text: the SDD states single-loop logic is a designed degraded mode with the warning still available, but does not state the aircraft-level effect (residual missed-detection or spurious-warning likelihood) needed to derive a severity. Deriving one would require a probability assumption the engineer must own.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection across monitored zones
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No fire or overheat warning available in any monitored zone (engine nacelles, APU, bleed ducts, gear bays, hold); any fire or overheat progresses undetected and the crew-commanded extinguishing path is never triggered, permitting uncontrolled fire in fire zones containing flammable fluid and high-energy sources.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no fire/overheat warning at all; no protective or extinguishing action is initiated until secondary effects appear.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; freighter carries flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from effects: total loss of detection removes the warning that gates all crew extinguishing across every fire zone, permitting undetected uncontained fire and loss of the aircraft; PROPOSED for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent/erroneous extinguishant discharge into a non-fire zone
fha.effAc: Extinguishant released into a zone with no fire; agent consumed leaving reduced/no reserve for a genuine subsequent fire in that engine pair; possible transient effects of agent in the zone.
fha.effCrew: Spurious discharge indication; crew must reassess fire-protection availability and revise dispatch/diversion.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded from the function definition alone. Aircraft-level effect depends on (a) whether agent ingress affects engine operation or crew air, and (b) the residual protection state after the inadvertent discharge — both need architecture/agent data not in the provided function statement. Leaving severity empty rather than guessing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to discharge on valid crew fire-handle command
fha.effAc: Commanded extinguishing does not occur; a detected engine/APU fire is not suppressed, allowing continued burn with potential structural, fuel, or adjacent-system damage.
fha.effCrew: Crew pulls fire handle, receives no discharge / no fire-out; must attempt second shot or divert with an active fire.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. Failure to extinguish a valid, detected engine/APU fire leaves an uncontrolled fire in a high-energy, flammable-fluid zone; combined with the fire this can progress to loss of aircraft. Severity is conditional on coincident fire (a mitigating-function loss). Confirm against §25.1309 and the fire-zone architecture. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected agent depletion leaving reserve unavailable at time of need
fha.effAc: Extinguishing reserve unavailable when a fire occurs; a detected engine/APU fire cannot be suppressed (or a second shot is unavailable), allowing continued burn.
fha.effCrew: Crew commands discharge expecting protection; no agent available; must divert/land with an active or re-ignited fire.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. Undetected depletion is latent: the loss is unknown until the agent is needed, at which point a detected engine/APU fire cannot be extinguished — equivalent aircraft effect to failure-to-discharge, conditional on coincident fire. Confirm severity and the latency/exposure treatment against §25.1309. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of extinguishing in one engine pair
fha.effAc: Both nacelles of one engine pair lose extinguishing capability (bottles cross-plumbed within a pair); a detected fire in that pair cannot be suppressed, allowing continued burn in a fire zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew fire-handle action for that pair produces no fire-out; must shut down affected engine(s) and divert with an unsuppressed fire risk on that side.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. Because bottles are cross-plumbed per pair, loss of extinguishing for one pair removes suppression for both nacelles of that pair; combined with a fire in that pair the outcome can progress to loss of aircraft. Severity is conditional on coincident fire. Confirm against §25.1309. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of automatic APU discharge only
fha.effAc: Automatic APU-zone discharge on detection (with the aircraft unattended) is lost; an APU fire on the ground/unattended is not automatically suppressed. Engine extinguishing and manual APU protection remain unaffected.
fha.effCrew: On the ground/unattended there is by definition no crew present to command discharge; in flight the effect depends on whether manual APU discharge exists.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded from the function definition alone. The consequence hinges on whether automatic APU discharge is the sole protection for the unattended-ground case and what backup (manual/crew) exists — the provided function statement does not establish the aircraft-level effect. Leaving severity empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire extinguishing in engine and APU zones
fha.effAc: An engine or APU fire in a fire zone cannot be extinguished by the installed means; the nacelle/APU compartment is a fire zone with flammable fluid present and the wing carries integral fuel tanks. Detection remains but the crew has no means to suppress a detected fire; potential for uncontrolled fire, structural burn-through and spread toward the wing/fuel.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive the fire warning and actuate the fire handle to no effect; no further mitigation available in flight.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the means to extinguish a detected fire in a fire zone adjacent to flammable fluid and integral wing fuel tanks presents a path to uncontrolled fire and structural burn-through. PROPOSED Catastrophic — confirm; the fire-progression/survivability effect is engineering judgement and requires substantiation (the SDD states the design but does not assess fire spread). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous low oxygen delivery at a mask station under demand
fha.effCrew: One crew mask station delivers inadequate oxygen under demand; regulators are independent per mask and a crossover/second cylinder feed the manifold, so the affected crewmember can transfer to another station. During a depressurisation or smoke/fume event the affected crewmember experiences degraded protection until reconfiguration.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Regulators are independent per mask and the two-cylinder manifold with crossover supplies four stations, so a single erroneous station is recoverable by station transfer; degraded protection for one crewmember during a depressurisation/smoke event supports Major. PROPOSED — confirm; classification depends on the assumption that alternative stations remain available and detection allows transfer, which the SDD asserts as architecture but does not assess. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected supply/regulator degradation developing below low-pressure alerting
fha.effCrew: Supply/regulator degradation develops without annunciation; the crew continue duties unaware and do not act. On a subsequent depressurisation or smoke/fume event at altitude the crew find oxygen protection inadequate when it is demanded, with limited or no time to reconfigure.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected degradation defeats the crew's protection precisely when a depressurisation or smoke/fume event demands it, with the crew unaware and taking no action; inability of the crew to cope with a subsequent event supports Hazardous. PROPOSED — confirm; leans on the max operating altitude / diversion exposure the SDD asserts but does not quantify. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced oxygen supply/endurance at one or more mask stations
fha.effCrew: Oxygen endurance is reduced below the sized diversion duration; the system is sized for four occupants for the diversion time at max operating altitude with reserve, so reduced endurance erodes the reserve margin. Crew may face insufficient oxygen if a long diversion follows a depressurisation.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced endurance erodes the sized reserve for the diversion case while the primary protection function remains available; a significant reduction in safety margin supports Major. PROPOSED — confirm; whether the shortfall reaches Hazardous depends on the actual diversion time/altitude and remaining reserve, which the SDD sizes qualitatively but does not quantify. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of oxygen supply to crew mask stations
fha.effCrew: No breathing oxygen available at any mask station. On a depressurisation, smoke or fume event at altitude the crew have no protection and cannot sustain performance for the descent and diversion; risk of crew incapacitation with only two nominal crew.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of the crew's sole breathing-oxygen protection during a depressurisation/smoke/fume event at altitude threatens crew performance and risks incapacitation; PROPOSED Hazardous. Confirm — could rise to Catastrophic if coincident with a depressurisation is credited as the reference case; the SDD asserts the protection function and max altitude but does not assess crew incapacitation outcome. — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: Fuel, hydraulic, electrical power and wiring (FUE, HYD, EPS, EWS) are resources and are excluded from the aircraft function list.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD classifies these as resources that supply rather than act on the aircraft; the modeling rule forbids authoring resources as functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any resource must be treated functionally (e.g. fuel delivery as an aircraft function), an additional top-function and sub-functions would be added and the FCIM/FHA baseline would grow.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS from all add_function actions.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.text: The nose visor's structural load path is structure, so only the door's actuation/locking/sensing behaviours are authored as functions.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the door is a single load path treated as structure; structural integrity is a PRA/structural-analysis item, not a functional-FHA function.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the door structural closure is to be tracked functionally, a further function would be added; otherwise it belongs in PRA/structures.
assumptions.usedFor: Nose visor functions (actuate/lock, sense/indicate) — structural role excluded.

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: The top-level aircraft function groupings (e.g. 'Control aircraft trajectory', 'Decelerate on the ground') are my derivation, not stated in the SDD.
assumptions.rationale: Appendix A explicitly states the document does not enumerate the aircraft-level functions; the function list must be derived by the safety organisation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the intended aircraft function taxonomy differs, the grouping and sub-function up-links would be re-cut before AFHA.
assumptions.usedFor: Every funcName top-level grouping across all add_function actions.

citations.quote: It does not tell you what the aircraft-level functions are.

assumptions.text: All segregation/independence statements captured in the sub-function notes are installation claims to be verified by ZSA/CMA, not established independence.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states its schematics mark commonality as installation statements, not findings, and independence claims must be tested rather than assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a claimed separation is defeated in installation, the affected sub-function is not independently failable and the FHA/FTA structure changes.
assumptions.usedFor: Independence notes on FCS, LDG, NZD, ECS, IPS, AVI, FPR, OXY sub-functions.

citations.quote: a claim about independence that has to be tested rather than assumed

assumptions.text: Indication and mitigation fields are left empty because AFHA effects and detection means do not yet exist to ground them.
assumptions.rationale: The FCIM feeds the AFHA; crew-indication and mitigation detail cannot be grounded from the function list alone until effects/detection are established.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection means are already defined, the empty Indication/Mitigation fields would be populated, potentially collapsing an Unaware row.
assumptions.usedFor: All indication/mitigation fields on SF-001..SF-005 rows

citations.quote: It does not enumerate failure conditions. It does not classify anything by severity

assumptions.text: The alerting system provides a consolidated crew alert list, so many of these conditions would be crew-Aware once effects are defined.
assumptions.rationale: Provided document states an alerting list exists but does not map specific alerts to these functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a given condition has no associated alert and is not self-evident, its Unaware row set would grow.

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list

assumptions.text: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine is a combined condition against yaw control authority and is flagged for the Combined column.
assumptions.rationale: SDD identifies the outboard moment arm as the sizing case for directional control, coupling SF-001 loss to SF-005 demand.
assumptions.ifWrong: If directional control is not sized by this case, the SF-001↔SF-005 combined flag is removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001 asymmetric-thrust partial and Combined flag with SF-005

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: Loss of all fly-by-wire command paths reverts pitch trim and the lower yaw segment to a degraded mechanical mode, a combined pitch/yaw condition.
assumptions.rationale: SDD states a mechanical reversion path exists only to stabiliser trim and lower rudder segment, coupling SF-004 and SF-005 degraded states.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversion coverage differs, the SF-004/SF-005 degraded partials and Combined flag change.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004 and SF-005 outside-MAC partials and Combined flag

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: SF-006 provides both symmetric and asymmetric high-lift failure modes because the two power drive units feed a common torque shaft with section asymmetry brakes.
assumptions.rationale: The function list gives only 'Provide high-lift configuration'; the asymmetry-vs-symmetric split is grounded in the SDD architecture, not the function name.
assumptions.ifWrong: The asymmetric-deployment malfunction condition would be removed and the Combined-column flag with braking/steering would drop.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006 malfunctions[] asymmetric deployment; Aware and Unaware rows

citations.quote: driven by two independent power drive units through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.text: An asymmetry annunciation exists for high-lift, so gross asymmetry is crew-Aware while sub-threshold asymmetry retains a separate crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists 'asymmetry and jam discretes' as FCS outputs but does not define the detection threshold, so an undetectable variant cannot be excluded.
assumptions.ifWrong: If asymmetry detection covers all magnitudes the SF-006 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row.

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes; high-lift position to the performance computation

assumptions.text: SF-007 (ground load support / flotation) has no crew-Unaware failure condition because its degradation manifests as physical ground behaviour that is self-evident to the crew.
assumptions.rationale: Flotation/load-support loss produces evident ground effects; the SDD provides no covert-degradation mechanism, so the unaware case is inapplicable per-condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a covert structural or flotation degradation exists, an SF-007 Unaware row carrying that undetectable condition must be added.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-007 single Aware row, no Unaware row

citations.quote: absorbs landing and taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, spreads footprint pressure to the level

assumptions.text: Braking degradation can develop below crew detection before the brakes are applied, justifying an SF-008 crew-Unaware row on the semi-prepared strip.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not define a pre-application braking-health indication, so reduced effectiveness discoverable only on application is credible.
assumptions.ifWrong: If brake health is annunciated pre-application the SF-008 Unaware effectiveness condition is removed.

citations.quote: Brake temperature is monitored continuously and a turnaround limit is displayed

assumptions.text: The SF-010 in-flight lock-integrity-loss-while-indicating-locked condition is a distinct crew-Unaware failure because the door cannot be operated in flight yet lock status is a load-bearing display.
assumptions.rationale: Dual dissimilar sensing reduces but does not eliminate a common latent loss where indication still reads locked; the SDD does not claim sensing covers all lock-loss mechanisms.
assumptions.ifWrong: If sensing is proven to detect every lock-integrity loss, the SF-010 Unaware in-flight condition is removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010 Unaware malfunctions[] loss of lock integrity indicating locked

citations.quote: Lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times and is included in the take-off configuration check

assumptions.text: An erroneous 'locked' indication on SF-011 can present with the lock pins not actually driven, because the two dissimilar sensing paths could both misread pin state.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual dissimilar sensing but does not state the failure behaviour that produces a false-secure indication; this is needed to justify the crew-Unaware malfunction row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a false-secure indication is architecturally precluded, the SF-011 Unaware row and its malfunction condition are removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011 Unaware row (erroneous locked indication with pins not engaged)

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.text: The restraint tension monitoring loop can fail to annunciate a real restraint loss due to its single-loop coverage gap, producing a crew-unaware condition.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD flags loop coverage as a recorded item but does not state whether a coverage gap can mask a real loss; required to justify the SF-012 Unaware partial.
assumptions.ifWrong: If coverage is complete or a loop failure is itself annunciated, the SF-012 Unaware partial is removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012 Unaware row (undetected restraint loss with monitoring-loop coverage gap)

citations.quote: restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item

assumptions.text: A pressure-differential drift and an ECS contaminant/temperature excursion can each develop below the crew's detection threshold, justifying the SF-013 and SF-014 Unaware malfunction rows.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD provides differential/cabin-altitude indication but no detection thresholds or alerting logic, so the crew-Unaware split cannot be grounded and the indication field is left empty.
assumptions.ifWrong: If alerting reliably catches these excursions, the SF-013 and SF-014 Unaware rows are removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-013 and SF-014 Unaware malfunction rows

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics

assumptions.text: Loss/degradation of a stabiliser ice-protection zone is annunciated to the crew, making the degraded case crew-Aware.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states a lost electrical zone is annunciated but does not confirm the annunciation reaches the crew alerting list for stabiliser zones specifically.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-016 partial-loss condition would move from the Aware row to the Unaware row, changing detection assumptions the AFHA relies on.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016 Aware row partials[] 'loss of one or more stabiliser heating zones'

citations.quote: Electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated

assumptions.text: Probe/port heater faults are individually monitored and annunciated, so heater loss is crew-Aware while air-data corruption from undetected accretion is crew-Unaware.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD says heated elements are 'monitored individually' but does not state whether the monitor covers accretion-induced air-data error versus only element health.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-017 Unaware malfunction 'undetected probe or port icing corrupting air data' could move to Aware, altering detection means feeding SF-018.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017 Aware and Unaware rows; combined-condition flag with SF-018

citations.quote: windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually

assumptions.text: The alerting system's two independent channels cannot self-detect a missed (unannunciated) valid condition, so 'failure to annunciate' is genuinely crew-Unaware.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual processing channels but does not state cross-channel monitoring that would flag a missed alert to the crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-019 Unaware missed-alert conditions could be detectable and move to Aware, changing the mitigation credit available for downstream AFHA classification.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019 Unaware row malfunctions[] 'failure to annunciate a valid condition'

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.text: Fire/overheat AND-then-single-loop logic means a failure to detect an actual fire develops without a crew cue, making it crew-Unaware.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes loop logic and degradation but does not state a loop-integrity monitor that would warn the crew before a detection gap becomes a missed fire.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-020 Unaware missed-detection condition could be detectable via loop monitoring and move to Aware, changing the AFHA's indication substantiation.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020 Unaware row 'failure to detect an actual fire or overheat'

citations.quote: AND logic between them for warning, degrading to single-loop logic on loss of one loop

assumptions.text: Undetected probe icing (SF-017) feeding erroneous air data to the displays (SF-018) is a cross-function combined failure condition for the matrix Combined column.
assumptions.rationale: The two functions interact via shared air-data sensing but the FCIM rows are authored per-function; the combined condition needs the engineer to file it in the Combined column.
assumptions.ifWrong: If air-data sourcing is fully independent per display, the combined condition is not credible and would be removed from the Combined column.

citations.quote: pitot, static and angle-of-attack sensing

assumptions.text: The engine/APU fire extinguishing capability is credited only when a valid fire is present, so the crew-Aware total-loss condition assumes an existing fire warning as its detection context.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes detection and discharge but does not enumerate failure-condition detection means; the awareness split for extinguishing failure had to assume the fire warning is the triggering cue.
assumptions.ifWrong: If extinguishing failure can occur without an accompanying detection cue, the SF-021 Aware/Unaware split changes and an additional undetected total-loss condition is needed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-021 Aware total-loss and partials rows

citations.quote: Each engine nacelle and the APU compartment carry dual-loop continuous fire detection

assumptions.text: Agent depletion (inadvertent discharge or leakage) can occur without a dedicated crew annunciation, justifying a distinct crew-Unaware SF-021 malfunction row.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists discharge status output but does not state whether reserve/agent-quantity loss is annunciated, forcing an assumption to place the undetected condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If agent quantity is continuously monitored and annunciated, the SF-021 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row.
